content:
Let the track length be \(L\), and let \(T=\frac{2L}{v_{\max}}\) be the time when the fastest runner finishes.

For any blue-red pair with speeds \(u\) and \(v\), using unfolded positions:
\[
x_B(t)=L-|L-ut|,\qquad x_R(t)=|L-vt|.
\]
They meet exactly when
\[
|L-ut|+|L-vt|=L.
\]
Solving this:
- If both are on their first leg: \(t=\frac{L}{u+v}\).
- If both have turned: \(t=\frac{3L}{u+v}\), valid since all speed ratios are less than \(12/9=4/3<2\).
- If exactly one has turned, the meeting would require one speed to be more than twice the other, impossible here.

Thus every blue-red pair meets exactly twice.

Also,
\[
\frac{3L}{u+v}<\frac{3L}{18}=\frac L6<\frac{2L}{v_{\max}}=T,
\]
so both meetings happen before the fastest runner finishes.

There are \(5\cdot 5=25\) blue-red pairs, so the total number of checks is
\[
25\cdot 2=50.
\]

\[
\boxed{50}
\]
